skills.name: Point-slope form

steps.a: meaning of y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)
steps.b: write from a point and slope

skills.wrong_turn: The signs in the parentheses flip: through (2, −1) it's y + 1 = m(x − 2), not y − 1 = m(x + 2).
skills.rule: y−y1=m(x−x1) is the line with slope m through (x1,y1).

skills.name: Standard form
skills.wrong_turn: The x-intercept of 2x + 3y = 12 is 6, not 2. Set y = 0 and solve; don't read off a coefficient.
skills.rule: Ax+By=C, usually with integers A, B, C and A≥0.

skills.name: Converting forms

steps.d: pick the best form for a job

skills.wrong_turn: Converting to standard form, clear fractions from every term: (1/2)x − y = −4 times 2 is x − 2y = −8.
skills.rule: One line, three forms: y=mx+b, y−y1=m(x−x1), Ax+By=C.

skills.name: Horizontal & vertical lines
skills.wrong_turn: y = 3 is horizontal, not vertical. It's every point with height 3, running left to right.
skills.rule: y=k is horizontal with slope 0. x=h is vertical with undefined slope.

skills.name: Parallel lines

steps.c: write a parallel line through a point
steps.d: check sides are parallel on a grid (compare slopes)

skills.wrong_turn: Same slope isn't enough if the intercepts match too: y = 2x + 1 and 4x − 2y = −2 are the same line.
skills.rule: Distinct non-vertical lines are parallel exactly when their slopes are equal.

skills.name: Perpendicular lines

steps.c: write a perpendicular line through a point

skills.wrong_turn: The perpendicular slope to 2/3 is −3/2, not −2/3 or 3/2. Flip and change the sign.
skills.rule: Non-vertical lines are perpendicular exactly when m1m2=−1.

skills.name: Intercepts of lines
skills.wrong_turn: The x-intercept is a point on the x-axis, (15, 0), with y = 0. Don't set x = 0 to find it.
skills.rule: For the x-intercept set y=0; for the y-intercept set x=0.

skills.name: Two-variable inequalities

steps.c: check if a point is a solution

skills.wrong_turn: Don't shade by the direction of the sign alone. y > −x + 2 shades above, but −y > x − 2 shades below. Use a test point.
skills.rule: Graph the boundary line, then shade the side where a test point works.

skills.name: Linear regression & residuals

steps.a: line of best fit with technology

skills.wrong_turn: A high r doesn't prove one thing causes the other, and r near 0 doesn't mean no relationship, only no straight-line one.
skills.rule: The best-fit line makes the residuals, actual minus predicted, as small as possible overall.
